title: Obedience of Christ
definition: The obedience of Christ is His perfect submission to the Father's will in every thought, desire, word, action, suffering, and sacrifice.
summary: Jesus obeyed perfectly where sinners have failed.
christFocus: Christ's obedience provides righteousness for His people and becomes the pattern of faithful discipleship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus obeyed the Father perfectly. His obedience was not outward only, but complete from the heart. He fulfilled righteousness in every area of life.

His obedience is essential to salvation. Sinners need forgiveness for disobedience, but they also need righteousness. Christ's obedience is counted to those who trust Him.

The obedience of Christ also teaches believers how to live: not by self-will, but by trust, love, submission, and dependence on the Father.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often think only of Christ's death and forget His righteous life. This doctrine matters because salvation includes both sins forgiven and righteousness provided in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in the obedience of Christ for your standing before God. Then follow His example by submitting your will to the Father in daily life.
